messages:
Ash: quick follow-up from today's memory incident postmortem — putting a concise owner + ETA list here. need owners by EOD so we can scope next sprint. TL;DR: recurring OOMs on inference workers after ~48-72h due to per-shard resident growth + heap fragmentation, not a single big allocation.

Ash: action proposals (please react with :thumbsup: or claim):
  1) deep sampling + allocation heatmap (heap profiles, jemalloc stats) — owner? ETA 3d
  2) add eviction/limit guardrails for long-lived shards (config + canary) — owner? ETA 1w
  3) investigate fragmentation pattern and tune tcache/jemalloc arenas — owner? ETA 2w
  4) dashboard + alert for steady-state drift (sustained > X MB over 6h) — owner? ETA 3d
  5) oncall runbook update + repro steps + perf tests — owner? ETA 5d

Maya: I'll take 1) heap profiles. will run continuous pprof snapshots + jemalloc stats across a few bad hosts. planning initial findings by Thu.

Kevin: I'll pick 3) allocator tuning and the eviction guardrails (2). can prototype a per-shard soft limit with a fallback eviction policy. aim to have a canary by next Tue.

Lia: I'll own 4) dashboards and 5) runbook edits. I'll add a drift panel and an alert that triggers a paging policy if growth rate > 50MB/hr for 6h. ETA end of week for dashboards, runbook update next Wed.

Ash: thanks. can we get a short checklist for Maya's profiling run so others can reproduce? also include exact commands you run so infra can attach heap dumps to tickets.

Maya: sure — sample command set below (will attach full script to the ticket):
```
# capture jemalloc stats + heap profile every 5m for 24h
for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=infer -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  kubectl exec $p -- sh -c 'echo "jemalloc.stats"; cat /proc/$$/status || true' > /tmp/jemalloc_$p.txt
  kubectl cp $p:/var/profiles/heap.pprof ./heap_$p_$(date +%s).pprof || true
done
```
I'll also enable malloc_conf for a subset of canaries to expose arena usage.

Kevin: if malloc_conf changes are needed, let's gate them behind a toggle and only roll to dedicated pools. also we should add a micro-benchmark that stresses long-lived sessions to verify fragmentation regressions.

Ash: good call. Kevin, can you add the micro-bench to the 'inference-load' repo and link the PR here when ready?

Kevin: will do. putting a TODO in the sprint board now. PR link when ready.

oncall-bot: incident-1923456789: scheduled heap-sample job created for profile collection. next run in 2m.

Maya: quick note — initial low-hanging signal: per-shard LRU counters are drifting because TTLs aren't being applied consistently after model warmup. i'll instrument and confirm; if true we can mitigate quickly with a TTL enforcement patch (hotfix).

Lia: if there's a hotfix path, let's also add an automated rollback threshold in the canary to revert if memory climbs > 150% of baseline.

Ash: agreed. owners + written ETAs: Maya (heap profiles) Thu EOD; Kevin (allocator + eviction + micro-bench) Tue next week; Lia (dashboard + runbook) Fri/Wed. please update the ticket with links and tag me.

Kevin: noted. also adding perf/regression job that runs daily for the next 2 weeks after canary.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-1452 "memory drift followup — profiles + guardrails" and linked incident. assignees: Maya, Kevin, Lia.

Ash: last item — let's have a sync in 4 days to review concrete numbers (heap delta, fragmentation ratio, canary results). pinging here: @Maya @Kevin @Lia — can everyone make a quick 30m slot then?

Maya: yes, I'll block 30m Thu morning.

Kevin: fine for Tue afternoon (after canary). if we need earlier, I can rearrange.

Lia: Thu morning ok for me.

Ash: cool. I'll schedule the sync and put the agenda in the calendar: 1) profiling findings, 2) canary plan, 3) dashboard thresholds, 4) runbook + paging changes.

Maya: uploading initial pprof snapshots to INF-1452 now. will add a short summary when I finish the first pass.

Ash: thanks all — this is actionable. please mark the ticket when you hit checkpoints so we can close the postmortem loop. :white_check_mark:
